components.summary: The declared-intent contract for living artifacts: artifacts declare verbs as data, and clicks on inert markup dispatch real backend work. ArtifactAction is the declaration — local kinds (choice/toggle/delete) mutate content through the same upsert→push path agent writes use, while intent kinds carry a stable binding ID the gateway resolves against the pinned revision; the intent name travelling with the artifact is display and debugging material, never the thing to run. HTMLArtifactIntentBridge is the only way out of untrusted content: a trusted click on data-hermes-binding markup becomes a nonce-gated private-scheme navigation in an isolated content world — synthetic clicks rejected, no message handler, fetch, or credential exposed — and native mirrors status back onto data-hermes-status attributes in the same world with a closed token vocabulary the page can style but not forge. ArtifactStore owns dispatch: slots keyed artifact/binding/entity so sibling rows report independently, idempotency keys reused per slot so a retry cannot execute twice, confirmation challenges bound server-side to actor, revision, binding, and expiry, and ledger rehydration seeding only terminal outcomes without overwriting live in-session state. IntentInvocationState.unsupported carries a reason distinguishing the four ways no handler ran — the artifact isn't in the local store, no gateway connection, a gateway with no artifact.action.invoke method at all, and a successful round trip whose binding has no registered handler — and each refusal is logged at notice, because the page has already swallowed the click and a silent refusal is indistinguishable from a dead control. MaintainerRef separates an artifact a cron actively tends from one that is merely mutable, and ArtifactIntentSessionLink lets native chrome post the session switch for an intent that ran as a contained session — reusing the same in-process notification the sidebar and inbox use, never handing the untrusted page a session ID or any navigation capability. HTMLPointerLockBridge hosts mouse capture for immersive worlds: trusted gestures only, offered at every stage of the gesture because WebKit treats pointerdown and click differently, gated by canvas dominance so a report's chart cannot eat the cursor, with a drag-look shim that translates locked movement into the drag a pre-contract page was written for.

Distinguish the four unsupported paths — local store miss, no connection, gateway without the method, gateway verdict — with per-path reasons surfaced to every display site
Gate the bridge out of untrusted HTML behind a per-view nonce in an isolated content world; only a trusted click on data-hermes-binding markup can carry the capability
Mirror invocation status onto data-hermes-status with a closed token vocabulary the page can style but not observe or override
Parse maintainer references so an artifact a cron actively tends is distinguishable from one-off authorship
Post session click-through from native code only, reusing the shared session-switch notification
Rehydrate terminal outcomes from the gateway's invocation ledger without overwriting live in-session state
flows: Each refusal on the dispatch path is logged at notice — local guards, the missing-method case, and the gateway's unsupported verdict each say which gate closed

components.summary: Living artifact presentation. ArtifactKindRenderer is the one place that decides how an artifact of any kind is drawn and — for interactive HTML — whether the host captures the mouse for it. The renderer's contract for live artifacts is that the action manifest travels with the artifact id: an html artifact declares its intents on the record rather than in its content, so passing actionableArtifactID without topLevelActions injects the intent bridge, captures the click, and resolves it against an empty manifest — the exact shape of a regression that left every control dead in the macOS side panel (the primary way an artifact is opened) and the iOS sheet while the expanded overlay worked. The surfaces that open a live artifact forward both: the transcript panel, the iOS artifact sheet, the expanded overlay, and the fullscreen window's intent context. Inline intent clicks are gated twice in the host — the negotiated capability set must advertise an artifact.action surface, and the binding must resolve against the declared manifest — and both refusals are logged at notice, because the page has already swallowed the click and a dead control otherwise looks identical to missing markup. Status display prefers the unsupported reason over the generic harness sentence at every site: the renderer's inline status row and the fullscreen window's status line both show IntentInvocationState's reason first, so copy names the gate that actually closed — a local miss, no connection, a gateway too old for the method, or a gateway verdict — instead of pointing at a server that was never asked. Status is also reflected back onto the page: every live intent slot for the artifact becomes a data-hermes-status mark, so each inert control reflects its own outcome independently of the one last clicked. HTML artifacts that declare actions but place no inline markers fall back to ArtifactTopLevelActionBar — trusted SwiftUI chrome above the document, no JS bridge involved. Blueprints enter the renderer's kind table the way every native block kind does: a ```blueprint fence or a stored blueprint artifact renders through BlueprintBlockView, which preserves the coordinates and dimensions its author declared on a logical canvas instead of asking a layout to infer placement — the deliberate opposite of the graph and Mermaid renderers, where the renderer owns geometry. The kind is registered at every site the other kinds are: ArtifactKindRenderer's dispatch, the ruler glyph in the canvas, fullscreen, transcript, panel, and thought-graph icon tables, and the structural preview gist that counts surviving elements and reads the title.

Fall back to trusted native action chrome when an HTML artifact declares actions but places no inline markers
Render blueprint artifacts and fences through BlueprintBlockView, preserving authored coordinates on the declared logical canvas rather than inferring layout
Register the blueprint kind at every shared site — renderer dispatch, ruler glyphs, and the element-count preview gist — so a blueprint is never an unknown kind on any surface

components.summary: Value types and wire/domain models shared across user experiences and service adapters. Cron job organization is modeled by CronCategory, which derives arbitrary-depth category paths from a job's own name and owns the display-name rules every surface shares. The dataflow graph now has an identity you can quote: CronGraphDigest is a SHA-256 content address over a canonical, byte-sorted, length-prefixed form of the graph as configured — schedule, enabled, usesLLM, deliver, description, and every edge are in, while lastStatus and health are out so the 10-second health poll cannot mint revisions — and layoutForm, a strict subset kept in the same file because the difference is the point, answers only whether a refresh must re-run the force layout. CronGraphRevisionStore keeps the append-on-change observation log: per-observation UUID identity so a revert A → B → A is three entries, runtime state stripped before storing so over(revision.graph) == revision.digest holds forever, capped at 200 revisions for disk. CronGraphDiff reports typed, human-phrased statements — rename versus refile told apart by leaf and path, edges as dataflow — with affectedNodeIDs, addedEdgeIDs, and removedEdges derived from the statements so the drawer and the canvas cannot drift. CronChangeset is the gateway-recorded counterpart carrying what the observed log structurally cannot: real time, an actor (human/agent/scheduler/other/unknown), and provenance turns. CronGraph itself is Codable for local snapshots only; gateway decoding stays on decodeGatewayValue. GatewayCapabilities is the negotiated-capability value the feature gates read: supportsArtifactActions, supportsActionLog, and supportsLearning hide their features when the set is silent, while supportsGatewayRestart is deliberately inverted — a gateway that reported nothing still gets the restart button, because restart is the recovery control and hiding it is how you end up needing shell access on the host; a gateway that did report and didn't list restart is taken at its word. The negotiated set is displayed by no view, so diagnosticSummary renders it as a pure, testable one-line verdict — the count, a loud supported/ABSENT artifact-actions flag, sorted names (or "none listed" so an empty set doesn't render as a bare colon) — which GatewayCapabilitiesStore logs at notice when capabilities resolve, the first place to look when a feature silently isn't there. BlueprintSpec is the wire contract for the same family's newest kind: the JSON body of a ```blueprint fence, decoded against a declared logical canvas (100 × 100 by default, each axis clamped to 10–1000) where every x/y/width/height is author-placed. Decoding is total where it can be — kind and style strings match case-insensitively and fall back to generic and flow — and sanitizing where integrity matters: element ids are trimmed with empties dropped and duplicates resolved first-wins, geometry clamps into the canvas with non-finite values collapsing to the minimum, and a connection survives only when both endpoints exist and differ. A spec whose elements all vanish parses as nil so the view shows its parse-error card instead of an empty drawing, and parsing is memoized through the shared RenderMemo (32 entries) like every other block spec. As a living artifact, a blueprint re-emit takes ArtifactMerge's default replace path — the incoming document replaces the stored one wholesale, the same semantics charts and timelines have.

components.summary: Hermes WebSocket JSON-RPC transport and Hermes Standard HTTP/SSE management APIs. GatewayClient now also speaks the gateway's recorded cron configuration history: cron.changesets (paged, filterable by since/until/job) and cron.changeset_diff (the graphs on either side of one recorded change). Conformance to CronChangesetSource is unconditional and deliberately says nothing about whether a given gateway implements the methods — that is CronChangesetFeed's runtime question, answered from the error the gateway returns. Decoding follows the wiki changesets' tolerant discipline over AnyCodable: every field is optional except id so a gateway need not have shipped the newest field for its history to be readable, a row missing its id is dropped rather than defaulted into existence, an empty parent_digest string is normalized to nil so it cannot chain a change to a revision that does not exist, and a graph that is present but malformed throws rather than decoding to nothing — the two failure shapes lead to different words on screen.
responsibilities: Decode changeset rows tolerantly: optional fields, dropped rows, nil-normalized parent digests, malformed graphs throwing

components.summary: Persistence, export, media, notifications, caching, reasoning, and device-local support services. CronChangesetSource is the capability seam for cron configuration history: a protocol rather than a version sniff, with two halves that are both needed — the protocol says the client speaks the RPC and lets a test hand over a source that does record history, while CronChangesetFeed.Availability says whether this gateway answers at runtime. cronChangesetDiff deliberately returns graphs rather than statements, so Portal derives the same CronGraphDiff sentences it derives for its own observed log instead of maintaining two dialects of "what changed", and CronChangesetDiff.structural(parentDigest:) applies the revision store's verbatim nil rule: a missing before graph is the empty graph only when the change had no parent at all, otherwise the comparison is honestly unavailable. SessionPDFExporter's ExportBlockView mirrors MarkdownContentView's block dispatch with export-safe substitutions, and blueprint fences join the short list rendered by the live view itself: BlueprintBlockView is pure SwiftUI + Canvas with an intrinsic aspect ratio, so ImageRenderer can rasterize it synchronously — unlike the async mermaid layouts that must be pre-rendered to images before the pass, and unlike the interactive chart whose scroll-view plot rasterizes as an empty box and is re-emitted non-interactive for export.
responsibilities: Carry the cron.changeset_diff payload — before/after graphs plus an optional unified text diff — with the honest nil rule for a missing parent graph

components.summary: Session, cron, activity, feed, skill, settings, gateway-lifecycle, learning, and file-browser state machines. CronGraphViewModel drives the interflow graph simulation: categoryHulls groups cron nodes by top-level folder (folders with two or more jobs), hulled folders are cached in hulledCategoryFolders whenever the published graph changes, displayLabel(forKind:label:) resolves canvas text per node, and a hosts edge is classified as containment — edgeIsContainment(_:), the muted service hue in edgeColor(forType:), and its edgeLegend placement. The commitment surface also lives here: digest is recomputed on graph didSet, both fetch paths funnel through a private adopt(_:) so whichever first notices a rewiring records it in the shared CronGraphRevisionStore, and CronGraphDigest.layoutForm replaces topologySignature for the rebuild-or-not decision so a schedule edit cannot scramble a settled layout. Reviewing a revision is a focus like a selection: reviewedRowID is a String so one selection serves both the observed log and gateway-recorded changesets, closing the drawer clears the review with it, and the diff is held rather than recomputed because the canvas redraws at 30 Hz. CronChangesetFeed keeps the honest account of asking the gateway — unsupported (method-not-found) never collapses into failed, and a failed refresh keeps already-fetched rows rather than silently demoting the drawer to observations.

components.summary: Sessions, cron, activity, skills, learning, mission-control, and the read-only Hermes file browser. The force-directed cron canvas now lives in CronGraphCanvas, extracted from CronInterflowGraphView with the wiki canvas's interaction model kept whole (NSView mouse interception on macOS, DragGesture on iOS, pinch zoom re-seeded per gesture). A review is drawn as a focus like a selection, reusing the existing dimming: changed nodes get a polarity-tinted ring outside the selection ring (dashed for removed), added edges draw at full strength with a halo, and removed edges are ghosted back along the shared curve — dashed, struck through, arrowless, in the warning tint. CronInterflowGraphView shows the graph's commitment as a copyable short-hash chip beside a history toggle that presents CronRevisionTimelineDrawer, which reads whichever log can answer: gateway-recorded changesets with real times, an actor chip, and the gateway's summary beside — never instead of — the derived statements, or Portal's own observations with the caveat in the header where it changes what every row below means. Which log is showing is one rows(recorded:observed:) decision so the title, caveat, and rows cannot disagree, and footnotes admit what the highlight couldn't reach on the current wiring.

components.summary: Reusable presentation primitives that no single product surface owns: chat skins, theme-aware controls, status surfaces, and presentation policy that stays testable without a running app. MacTopChrome is the pattern at its purest — a view-free enum whose one protected rule is that collapsing the chrome must never take the Back button away: mode(isSurfaceOpen:isCollapsed:) lets an open surface override the user's stored collapse preference because the surface header owns Back and its Escape shortcut, and height(for:) maps the mode to the 40pt expanded / 22pt collapsed row so callers never branch on the raw preference. ContentView holds the @AppStorage preference and applies mode and height to the row above the split view. The skin seam is ChatSkinProviding — messageBubble(message:persona:) renders every chat bubble on every surface, which is how a dashboard canvas panel draws bubbles identically to the full-screen transcript. PortalProgressView is the macOS-safe SwiftUI-native spinner (avoiding the flattened-AppKit-adaptor diagnostic), PortalButtonStyle draws every color from the active ButtonTheme palette, FlowLayout wraps tag chips, and StreamingStatusBar is the TUI-aligned braille spinner with state label and live tool calls.

components.summary: The agent-execution dashboard: the flamechart, the session canvas that rearranges a live chat into per-turn lenses, the free-form panel canvas, and the conversation panel that renders the live transcript as one more dashboard panel. ThoughtGraphView is the interactive flamechart of the react loop — horizontal position is when a step happened, bar width is how long, each actor owns a lane stacked by spawn order — and carries an explicit legacy-giant header: split tracked as debt, do not add to the file. SessionChatCanvas drives lenses by CanvasDisplayMode: scroll streams the live turn, turns pages one settled turn at a time, and only the per-turn lenses and the conversation focus change between modes. DashboardCanvasView is deliberately content-agnostic — z-order is layout-array order, frames live in the canvas's own coordinate space, and layout persists via onLayoutCommitted on drag-end so UserDefaults writes stay off the per-frame path — and PanelContext hands every panel builder the same material: the turn's composed nodes, compaction folds, skills, the shared cross-highlight selection, and the single flamechart engine. The conversation panel's live tool calls are the newest load-bearing rule: ChatMessage.toolCalls is stamped once at message.complete, so during a running turn the records live only in ChatViewModel.activeToolCalls — mergingLiveToolCalls(into:activeToolCalls:) merges them into the streaming message before the peel bar and tools card are built, which is what makes the Tools chip and card exist while tools run instead of every tool appearing at once when the turn ends; the merge guards on message.isStreaming so a settled turn keeps its own stamped history rather than borrowing the next turn's in-flight records, and liveToolCallOrder sorts by startedAt with an id tiebreak because dictionary values rehash on every insert — sorting is what stops the rows reshuffling under the cursor on each tool event. Each turn's thinking and tools are peelable cards (PeeledBlockKind) anchored under the bubble — the card is the block's only render site, so the bubble is stripped of reasoning and the streaming status line does not re-list tools; nothing renders twice. The transcript is an eager VStack over a bounded 60-message tail window (lazy layout was the engine of a sampled 100%-CPU relayout loop), the live-tail follow is coalesced to one unanimated scroll per 150ms, and re-rendering is driven by ChatViewModel publishes, never a timer.
